expectation: CAIX is a membrane (and some cytoplasmic) stain on hypoxic tumour epithelial cells. It should appear in patches: regional zones of tumour nests, often near necrosis, that are strongly positive while other areas and other images are negative. Stroma and immune cells should be negative.
observed: A: images differ a lot. Several are negative. Three show honeycomb-like membrane outlines around cell nests, and one has a large solid bright zone at its lower edge. B and C (typical density) show only faint speckle. D: bright yellow surrounds dark nuclear holes.
why: Some images, and zones within them, show strong membrane outlines around cell nests while others are negative, which is the patchy hypoxic-tumour pattern expected of CAIX.
notes: Several images show honeycomb membrane staining of cell nests, with dark nuclei inside bright rings in D. Other images and fields B and C are near-negative, which fits regional hypoxia. The bright zone at one image's edge needs caution.
